drug.name: Oral Buprenorphine-based Medication Assisted Therapy Office-Based Opioid Treatment

source.list: Oral Buprenorphine-based Medication Assisted Therapy Office-Based Opioid Treatment Criteria

criteria.text: Patient is at least 16 years old.
First 28 days of newly initiated MAT OR buprenorphine/naloxone at ≤24 mg/day OR PA treatment-plan, support, product and denial criteria satisfied.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Oral Buprenorphine Criteria: Version 2 Approved 09/21/2018, Effective 11/12/2018, Revised 4/21/2023 (standards of care); Version 2.1 Revised 5/19/2023 (PA criteria). Rules engine only; no TypeSafe.

No-PA arms: patients new to buprenorphine MAT within the most recent 60 days have no PA requirement for the first 28 days when initiating therapy; buprenorphine/naloxone ≤24 mg buprenorphine/day requires no PA. Above 24 mg/day requires PA. Age ≥16 and opioid dependence apply to all encoded arms; treatment-plan adherence, prescriber qualifications, other-opioid exclusion and single-ingredient pregnancy restriction apply on the PA arm.

Standards of care framework: accessibility, comprehensiveness, coordination and continuity. Includes patient-centric options, barriers to treatment, initial/follow-up care, behavioral health integration, HIV/Hep C screening and treatment, family planning, prenatal care, co-morbid conditions, family engagement, education, harm reduction and self-care; coordination with primary/specialty care, level-of-care escalation, social supports and peri-procedure planning; care management, team emphasis and exit/re-entry protocols.

Authorization (notes only): satisfactory Standards of Care Attestation application and commitment to minimum standards confers a 12-month prescriber blanket authorization; prescriptions filled during that period require no separate per-member PA. Otherwise individual PA may be authorized for up to 12 months and renewed. Prescribers failing to maintain standards must submit individual requests until deficiencies are resolved.

Prescriber responsibilities (notes only): if psychosocial support is provided elsewhere, maintain a coordinated shared care plan and copies with both practitioners; routinely screen for anxiety and mental health challenges and provide supportive access to care; establish a patient-centric chronic pain plan without opioids that optimizes non-opioid therapies; encourage Care Management Program (CMP) enrollment and refer as appropriate; request continuation authorization in time to prevent treatment interruption; maintain an up-to-date plan and review with the patient at least every six months, considering trial tapers to lower maintenance doses when stable and ready.

Maximum daily dose (notes only): buprenorphine (Suboxone/Subutex) 24 mg/day (three 8 mg films); Zubsolv 22.8 mg/day (two 11.4 mg tablets). PA is required above these thresholds. The source separately states a general buprenorphine/naloxone ≤24 mg no-PA pathway; the product-specific Zubsolv threshold requires manual review and is not numerically enforced by this partial pack.
Preferred medication: refer to the PDL at http://dhss.alaska.gov/dhcs/pages/pharmacy/medpriorauthoriz.aspx; no preferred-agent trial predicate is inferred from this referral.

Regulatory authority (notes only): 7 AAC 120.120, 120.130, 120.140; 42 USC 1396r-8; 42 CFR 456 Subpart K; 7 AAC 105.230(c) medical necessity, clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, adverse effects and service-specific requirements. Newly FDA-approved drugs in reviewed classes are subject to the same DUR standards, including preferred-agent trials absent documented clinical contraindication. Covered outpatient drugs must meet 7 AAC 120.110; FDA approval without established clinical benefit does not qualify.

References (notes only): 12 AAC 40.975 controlled-substance prescribing; Mullin D and Martin S, Primary Care of Patients with Opioid Use Disorder, Alaska Primary Care Association (2017); SAMHSA Buprenorphine Waiver Management and NP/PA waiver qualification resources; SAMHSA PEP18 Treatment Locator; Center for Substance Abuse Treatment, Clinical Guidelines for the Use of Buprenorphine in the Treatment of Opioid Addiction, TIP 40, DHHS (SMA) 04-3939 (2004). Archived source references and regulatory language are retained as provenance, not newly imposed predicates.

new_mat_first_28_days.label: New to buprenorphine MAT within the most recent 60 days and requesting the first 28 days of initiating therapy (no PA).

daily_buprenorphine_le_24mg.label: Receiving buprenorphine/naloxone at a daily buprenorphine dose of 24 mg or less (no PA; see Zubsolv dose note).

single_ingredient_buprenorphine.label: Requested product is single-ingredient buprenorphine (e.g., Subutex), rather than buprenorphine/naloxone.

mat_treatment_plan_on_record.label: Patient and prescriber have a defined MAT treatment plan, including functional goals, and projected timeline on record.

regular_psychosocial_support.label: Patient is receiving regular psychosocial support.

patient_pregnant_female.label: Patient is a pregnant female (required for single-ingredient buprenorphine on the PA path).

agreed_to_treatment_plan.label: Patient has agreed to adhere to the treatment plan.

prescriber_qualified_for_buprenorphine_m.label: Prescriber meets all qualifications to prescribe buprenorphine-based products for opioid dependence.

no_concomitant_other_opioids.label: No concomitant prescriptions for other opioids while receiving oral buprenorphine MAT.
